record.paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
record.original_question: Can the entropy-reduction results obtained for correlated repeated feedback actuation be applied or extended to derive quantitative bounds for additional performance measures of feedback-controlled systems, in particular the maximum attainable flux or the maximum attainable power?

evidence.quote: Another open question is the application or the extension of the results found in [13] to find bounds for other performance measures of feedback controlled systems, for example, the maximum attainable flux or power.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a feedback-controlled stochastic system in contact with a thermal reservoir, in which a controller performs repeated measurements of the system state and applies actuations based on those measurements. Assume the successive measurement-actuation steps are correlated (i.e., not statistically independent across repetitions), and suppose one has available a quantitative bound on the entropy reduction of the system per cycle achievable by such correlated repeated feedback actuation (extending Sagawa–Ueda-type relations to the correlated case).

Within this setting, derive quantitative bounds, in terms of the information-theoretic quantities (mutual information, transfer entropy, or related correlation measures) that govern the entropy reduction, for the following performance measures of the feedback-controlled system:

1. The maximum attainable steady-state probability flux J (e.g., the net rate of transitions across a given cut in state space, or the net particle/current flow induced by the controller).
2. The maximum attainable extracted power P (the rate at which work can be extracted from the thermal reservoir using the feedback controller).

Specifically: establish tight upper bounds J ≤ Φ(I) and P ≤ Π(I), where I denotes the relevant per-cycle information measure characterizing the correlated repeated actuation, and determine whether these bounds are saturable by an explicit protocol.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on stochastic thermodynamics of feedback control has produced general second-law-like inequalities relating extracted work and entropy reduction to mutual information (Sagawa–Ueda and extensions, including non-Markovian/correlated feedback). However, specific tight bounds on the maximum attainable flux or extracted power for systems with correlated repeated feedback actuation, of the form requested here, do not appear to have been established in a definitive form; recent work (e.g., 2025 entropic-balance results) refines the entropy/information inequalities but does not settle quantitative flux/power bounds. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Entropic balance with feedback control: information equalities and tight inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Recent framework using Markovian joint description of system and controller, refining entropy/information inequalities under correlated measurements.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work continues to refine information-thermodynamic inequalities for feedback control but focuses on entropy production rather than tight flux/power bounds.

status_evidence.title: Thermodynamics of feedback controlled systems
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes bounds on entropy reduction via repeated feedback actuation.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational entropy-reduction bounds for repeated feedback actuation, which the open problem proposes to extend to flux and power.

status_evidence.title: Universal bounds on entropy production inferred from observed statistics
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses universal entropy-production bounds from observable currents.
status_evidence.claim: Related thermodynamic-uncertainty-style bounds exist but do not directly give the requested correlated-feedback flux/power bounds.
